## Load library

```{r}
library(sf)
library(tidyverse)
library(terra)
library(fs)
library(tidyterra)
library(plotly)
```

## Load rasters

```{r}
ssp1 <- terra::rast("week3_data/wc2.1_10m_tmax_ACCESS-CM2_ssp126_2081-2100.tif")
ssp5 <- terra::rast("week3_data/wc2.1_10m_tmax_ACCESS-CM2_ssp585_2081-2100.tif")
month <- c("Jan","Feb","Mar","Apr","May","Jun","Jul","Aug","Sep","Oct","Nov","Dec")
names(ssp1) <- month
names(ssp5) <- month
names(ssp1) <- month
names(ssp5) <- month
```

## Load country file

```{r}
cities <- st_read("week3_data/World_Cities/World_Cities.shp")
names(cities)
head(cities)
```

## Filter to Australia

```{r}
country_cities <- cities %>% filter(CNTRY_NAME == "Australia")
```

## Make sure the CRS matches your rasters

```{r}
st_crs(country_cities)
```

## Attatch the city names and pivot long for ssp1

Attach the city names, so each row is labelled.
Pivot long, so instead of 12 month columns you get one Month column and one Temp column. This makes it easy to group, join and plot later.

```{r}
city_ssp1 <- terra::extract(ssp1, terra::vect(country_cities))
city_ssp5 <- terra::extract(ssp5, terra::vect(country_cities))
```

## Attatch the city names and pivot long

Attach the city names, so each row is labelled.
Pivot long, so instead of 12 month columns you get one Month column and one Temp column. This makes it easy to group, join and plot later.
drop_na() matters because a city on a coastal cell can return NA, and max() of all NAs gives -Inf.

```{r}
ssp1_long <- city_ssp1 %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  mutate(City = country_cities$CITY_NAME) %>%
  dplyr::select(-ID) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = Jan:Dec, names_to = "Month", values_to = "Temp") %>%
  drop_na()

ssp5_long <- city_ssp5 %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  mutate(City = country_cities$CITY_NAME) %>%
  dplyr::select(-ID) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = Jan:Dec, names_to = "Month", values_to = "Temp") %>%
  drop_na()
```

## Define "maximum"

Maximum temperature is defined as each city’s highest monthly mean daily maximum temperature in 2081-2100. Note that WorldClim’s tmax is already an average, so this is the hottest month’s average, not an absolute record.

```{r}
max_ssp1 <- ssp1_long %>% group_by(City) %>% summarise(SSP1 = max(Temp))
max_ssp5 <- ssp5_long %>% group_by(City) %>% summarise(SSP5 = max(Temp))
```

I defined maximum temperature as each city’s hottest month under each scenario, giving one value per city per scenario. I chose this because it captures peak heat exposure.

## Calculate the difference

Join the two scenarios by city and compute SSP5 - SSP1

```{r}
diff_df <- max_ssp1 %>%
  inner_join(max_ssp5, by = "City") %>%
  mutate(Difference = SSP5 - SSP1)

diff_df
```

## Descriptive statistics

```{r}
diff_df %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(Difference),
            sd = sd(Difference),
            min = min(Difference),
            max = max(Difference),
            IQR = IQR(Difference))
```

## Histogram of differences plot

```{r}
ggplot(diff_df, aes(x = Difference)) +
  geom_histogram(color = "black", fill = "white", binwidth = 0.5) +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = mean(Difference)),
             color = "blue", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(title = "Difference in maximum temperature, SSP5 minus SSP1 (2081-2100)",
       x = "Difference (°C)", y = "Frequency") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

```

## Bar chart per city plot

```{r}
ggplot(diff_df, aes(x = reorder(City, Difference), y = Difference)) +
  geom_col(fill = "firebrick") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "SSP5 minus SSP1 maximum temperature by city",
       x = "City", y = "Difference (°C)") +
  theme_classic()
```

## SSP1 vs SSP5 side by side

```{r}
both <- diff_df %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(SSP1, SSP5), names_to = "Scenario", values_to = "MaxTemp")

means <- both %>% group_by(Scenario) %>% summarise(mean = mean(MaxTemp))

ggplot(both, aes(x = MaxTemp, color = Scenario, fill = Scenario)) +
  geom_histogram(position = "identity", alpha = 0.5, binwidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(data = means, aes(xintercept = mean, color = Scenario), linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Maximum temperature by scenario, 2081-2100",
       x = "Temperature (°C)", y = "Frequency") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
```
